title: Write integration test for rocket new (webapp template)
description: Create an integration test that calls scaffold() for the webapp template and verifies the full directory structure, key files, and .agent/ setup are created correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: Test verifies directory structure exists (client/, server/)
Test verifies package.json exists in client and server
Test verifies .gitignore exists in project root
Integration test passes with npm test

steps.details: Create the test file. Import scaffold from lib/scaffold.ts. Note: this test will be slow (runs npm install) — consider skipping npm install in test mode or using a flag.

steps.description: Mock npm install and git init for speed
steps.details: To avoid actually running npm install in tests, mock execSync: vi.mock('child_process', () => ({ execSync: vi.fn() })). This lets the test run quickly without network access.

it('scaffolds webapp correctly', async () => { await scaffold('webapp', 'test-app', tmpDir, { auth: true }); expect(await fs.pathExists(path.join(tmpDir, 'client/package.json'))).toBe(true); expect(await fs.pathExists(path.join(tmpDir, 'server/.env.example'))).toBe(true); // ... more checks })
Verify that {{PROJECT_NAME}} in template files is replaced with 'test-app': const pkgJson = await fs.readJson(path.join(tmpDir, 'package.json')); expect(pkgJson.name).toBe('test-app')
Run `npm test` and verify scaffold integration tests pass.

technicalNotes: Mocking execSync prevents actual npm install from running in CI — test the template file structure, not npm install itself
